_comment: BTO sites that have been launched but are not yet built, hand-maintained.
A launched BTO is the one thing the Master Plan cannot tell this app. The
site is zoned RESIDENTIAL with a plot ratio, a plot ratio is not a height,
so outlook.ts reads it as 'no published ceiling' — which is honest and
useless, because HDB has announced the storeys and sold the flats. One
point and one number here turns that direction into a definite answer.
No polygon is drawn by hand. `at` only has to land inside the site; the
outline comes from the Master Plan parcel under it, which is authoritative
and stays right when the plan is rebuilt. Run `npm run check-bto` after
editing to see which parcel each point picked up.
`storeys` is the TALLEST block on the site, because the question this
answers is whether anything here can rise into a window's view, and the
tallest block settles it. `storeysLow` is the shortest, and is reported to
the reader so a range is never mistaken for one number. Leave a site out

sites.name: Lakeview Cascadia
sites.note: Five blocks, 18-40 storeys, Prime, bounded by Upper Thomson Road. HDB does not publish which block is which height, so `storeys` is the tallest. Point is OneMap's own for the project name, and lands in the vacant GPR 3.9 parcel 360 m west of Marymount MRT.
